title: Elmer James and O'Neil Spencer
summary: James was a Chick Webb bassist; Spencer was young and wild drummer of the Blue Rhythm Band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then what about Elmer James, the bass player?
Yeah, he was a bass player. He was with Chick Webb.
Yeah, I knew him very well. Nice fellow.
And I'd like to ask you about O'Neil Spencer, too.

Oh, that's my boy. O'Neil Spencer. I don't know when and how I met him, or where. It was in somebody's band. I don't know if it was... I don't know how you can work with people and don't know when was the first time you saw them or anything. Yeah, I knew Spencer very well. He was with the Blue Rhythm Band. And I knew him before he was with the Blue Rhythm Band. One of them things.
What kind of a person was O'Neil Spencer?
Oh, he was young and wild. I mean, he was wild. Very wild.
Yeah. Nice guy. But young and wild. What more can you say? He was that age, you know.
Well, he was with you with Kirby, wasn't he?
No. Bill Beason was working with Kirby, and Walter Fuller [SIC: He means Wallace Bishop, who also had played with Earl Hines], he was with Kirby. That's all the drummers he had when I was there.
Yeah, when you were there. Okay. Because I think Spencer was there when Procope was there.
